Introduction

These are the developer docs: the internal API of 3code as extracted from the source by nim doc, every module, type, and proc with its doc comment. Where the manual shows you how to use the app and the reference lists every switch and config key, this half is for people embedding 3code in another program, writing a plugin, or changing 3code itself.

Start from the entry points:

  • threecode - the root module: entry point, outer REPL loop, and the full module list
  • index of every symbol - flat, alphabetical, one page

Embedding

The headless frontend is threecode/library: it runs the same agent loop, tools, sandbox, and .3log sessions as the CLI, with the terminal replaced by return values and callbacks.

import threecode/library

let s = initAgentSession(AgentOptions(model: "deepinfra.deepseek-v3.2"))
echo s.prompt("what does this project do?")
s.close()

Module tour

The modules a host or contributor touches most, with their job in one line:

modulewhat lives there
turnsturn lifecycle orchestration
actionstool dispatch: model tool_call JSON into Actions, then execute
snapgoal-mode tree manifest: arm at the mode, re-walk after bash, fold shell mutations into the change log
apiHTTP client and SSE parsing
sessionsession persistence in the .3log format
configconfig file parsing and provider/profile resolution
typesshared types and process-level globals
enginestateful terminal layout engine
minlinemultiline line editor
displaytranscript formatting: markdown, receipts, banners
webfetch and search helpers exposed as native tools

The root module's list also carries the newer surfaces (library for embedding, the plugin ABI, the sandbox and ACP frontends) and the long tail of wire translations, auth flows, and terminal internals.

Development guidelines

Rules that keep the interactive front ends responsive. They bind every change that adds or touches a : command.

A system command must never block

A : command runs while the user waits at the prompt (or queued behind a running turn), so it must return immediately — no network call, no model call, no long local work on the controller or input thread. Anything slower than a file read or a config write runs on a separate thread, and its result is delivered asynchronously afterwards, exactly like a normal one: the answer is committed to scrollback whenever it lands, and the tokens it burned are added to the session ledger and the token bar (the sum of both requests), not dropped because the call was async.

:btw is the pattern (see btwthread.nim): the command builds its request from the live history on the controller thread (the only place the history is stable), hands plain strings to a worker, and answers with no body of its own: the controller commits the ?-led question item in place of the echoed command line. The controller polls the job from its input wait (ui.deliverFinishedBtw) and commits the answer — dim, under the aside's ! icon, beneath the ? question item that replaced the echoed command line — between keystrokes. The worker's wire policy (btwRequest) is the main transport's in miniature: 429/5xx/transport failures and an empty 200 back off and retry, and an interrupt cancels the aside by comparing interruptsSeen() counts (the flag itself is cleared when the next turn starts); a cancelled worker's blocked HTTP call runs out on the retired list so later answers never queue behind it. Synchronous-by-contract surfaces (the library's command()) are the one exception: they join the worker and fold the answer into their return value, because their whole API blocks by design.

Regenerating

These pages are generated, never hand edited. The doc comment in the source is the text; nimble devdocs rewrites docs/dev/ from src/:

nimble devdocs

Note: The API here is internal. It serves readers of the source and embedders who accept churn; nothing on these pages is a compatibility promise.
